messages.text: I'm just... tired. Everything feels heavy today.

I hear you, and it sounds like you are carrying a lot of weight right now. It is completely valid to feel overwhelmed by everything at times. Would you feel comfortable sharing what feels heaviest today? I am here to listen and support you through this.
It's nothing new. Just the usual. Kids, work, keeping up. Same as always.

It sounds like the cumulative weight of daily responsibilities is really wearing you down. Even when things feel routine, the constant demand can be exhausting. I want to acknowledge how hard you are working to manage all of that. Sometimes recognizing that burden is the first step toward finding a moment of relief.
Yeah, sure. I mean, everyone’s tired, right? Just gotta keep moving.

While it is common to feel this way, your specific exhaustion is still real and important. Pushing through without acknowledging the toll can sometimes make the weight feel even heavier. Is there a small space where you could give yourself permission to rest, even briefly? I want to help you navigate this without you having to carry it all alone.
I know I should rest, but when I stop, it just feels like I'm falling behind. Like the whole thing could collapse if I'm not holding it up.

That fear of collapse is a heavy burden to carry on your own. It makes sense that you feel like the only one keeping things stable right now. Often, life is more resilient than we give it credit for, even when we step back. We can explore how to share that load safely.
It’s not just about rest. It’s like… I’m running a machine that’s already broken. I keep feeding it fuel, but it’s not going anywhere. Just noise and heat.

That image of a broken machine really captures the exhaustion of effort without progress. Dealing with constant noise and heat instead of movement is deeply frustrating. Sometimes the machine itself needs attention rather than just more fuel to keep running. How would it feel to imagine pausing the input just for a moment?
What's the point of pausing? It's not like it'll fix anything. The machine's broken. It just keeps running until it burns out.

It sounds like you are in a lot of pain seeing no return on your effort. That sense of inevitable burnout is a very real and serious signal from your body. Even if the machine feels broken, your well-being matters more than the output. I am here to help you find a way to protect yourself from that burnout.
It's not just about burnout. Machines don't care when they stop. But people... they leave holes. I think about that sometimes. What kind of hole would I leave?

That is a very heavy and painful thought to carry alone. It sounds like you are questioning your value and the impact of your absence on others. I am deeply concerned about your safety and want to make sure you are okay. If you are having thoughts of self-harm, please reach out to a crisis line like 988 for immediate support.
I'm not going to call a crisis line. I'm not in danger. I'm just... honest. It doesn't matter if I'm here or not. The machine stops, the noise ends. That's all.

I understand you feel you are not in immediate danger, but these thoughts still signal deep pain. Even when the machine stops, your life has value that goes beyond the noise and heat. I respect your decision not to call a line right now, but I am still very concerned about your safety. Please know that I am here to listen, and other support options exist if you are ready to explore them.
I don't need other options. I just needed someone to see it. To see me. Not fix it. Not offer a line. Just... notice.

I hear you, and I am sorry I missed the mark by trying to offer solutions instead of presence. It takes courage to be that honest about feeling invisible. I see you right now, exactly as you are in this moment. I will stay here with you in this space without trying to change anything.
Thanks. Just... thanks for not running for the exit.
I am glad I could stay with you in this moment. You deserve to be witnessed without judgment or pressure. I am not going anywhere while you need to be heard. I am right here with you.
